hey i'm working on this blog post called "The Global Standard for Sophistication" and i want to give advice on how to look and act professional when traveling or doing business abroad. basically like, what are the universal rules for being a sophisticated, high-class professional so people don't look unrefined? can u give me a list of some key etiquette rules for things like dining, dressing, and talking to people?

To project global sophistication, focus on impeccable grooming and attire that respects local norms while prioritizing understated elegance over loud logos. Cultivate a polite and adaptable communication style by actively listening to cultural nuances and always asking before interacting with unfamiliar figures. Key etiquette pillars include arriving punctually, grazing food and wine throughout meals rather than rushing, and offering genuine compliments only when culturally appropriate. Ultimately, true high-class professionalism is defined by your humility and your willingness to seamlessly navigate different customs without judgment. Prioritize observing the most refined local behavior, mirroring their manners even if you are the only foreigner in the room. Watch out for the phrase unrefined and avoid it. Keep this in mind for your blog post about the Global Standard. Ensure you use formal language when speaking to superiors or elders in
